title: X3 Configure the Project
subtitle: 10:25–11:05 · 40 minutes
description: Create a Project with fields and three views, add three justified milestones, and record one blocking dependency.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **Time:** 40 minutes
- **You produce:** a Project linked to your repository with the fields Status, Priority, Start date, Target date, and Basis; the views Backlog, Board, and Roadmap; three milestones with justified dates; and one "blocked by" dependency.
- **New terms:** [Project](../cheat-sheet.qmd#project), [milestone](../cheat-sheet.qmd#milestone), [view](../cheat-sheet.qmd#view), [field](../cheat-sheet.qmd#field), [Project workflow](../cheat-sheet.qmd#project-workflow), [dependency](../cheat-sheet.qmd#dependency). All terms are in the [cheat sheet](../cheat-sheet.qmd).
:::

## Why this step

Issues describe the work. A **Project** shows the work as a plan: what is waiting, what is in progress, and what happens when. A Project belongs to your account, not to the repository. You link it to the repository, and you set its **visibility separately**. A public repository can have a private Project, and the reverse.

A plan needs time. GitHub offers two different tools for time, and they answer different questions. A **milestone** groups Issues under one due date in the repository: "What must be ready for the registration?" **Date fields** in the Project give each Issue a start and a target: "When do I work on this?" The **roadmap** shows both together.

Finally, order matters. "Submit the registration" cannot start before "Check the registration requirements" ends. This is a **dependency** ("blocked by"), not a hierarchy. A parent-child relation says "this is part of that"; a dependency says "this waits for that". Keep the two apart.

Milestone dates need a justification. The fictional registration (2026-12-01) and submission (2027-06-01) stand in for official dates of the Dean's Office; the six months between them follow the [DH study plan, Art. 15 Abs. 4](../../documentation/requirements.qmd). The middle milestone is your own estimate, and you may move it. Never move an official date silently.

## Before you start

- You finished [X2](x2.qmd).
- Look at the [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) for orientation.

## Steps

### Create the milestones

1. Click **Issues**, then **Milestones**, then **New milestone**.
2. Type the title `M1 Registration submitted` and the due date `2026-12-01`.
3. In **Description**, write the justification from the [milestone list](../../project-management/milestones.md).
4. Click **Create milestone**.
5. Repeat for `M2 Data documented and validated` (2027-03-01, proposed) and `M3 Thesis submitted` (2027-06-01).
6. Open each sub-issue and set its milestone in the sidebar: E01 tasks → M1, E08-S1 and E08-T2 → M2, E08-T3 → M3.

{{< screenshot x3-milestones >}}

### Create and link the Project

1. Open the **Projects** tab of your repository.
2. Click **New project**.
3. Select the **Table** layout. Name the Project `PROJM thesis plan`.
4. Click **Create project**.
5. Open the Project menu (**…**, top right) and select **Settings**.
6. Check **Visibility**: public for the public path, private for the private path.

**Fast route:** open the [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11), open its menu (**…**), and select **Make a copy**. The copy has all fields and views but no Issues. Then link it to your repository (**Projects** tab → **Link a project**).

### Add the Issues

1. In the Project table, click **+** at the bottom (or press `Ctrl`+`Space`).
2. Type `#`, select your repository, and select the epic E01.
3. Repeat for E08.
4. The default workflow **Auto-add sub-issues to project** adds the sub-issues. If they do not appear, add them the same way.

### Create the fields

1. In the table header, click **+** and select **New field**.
2. Create `Priority` as **Single select** with the options `High`, `Normal`, `Low`.
3. Create `Basis` as **Single select** with the options `Rule`, `Practice`, `Demo`.
4. Create `Start date` and `Target date` as **Date**.
5. Open the settings of the field **Status**. Set the options to `Backlog`, `Ready`, `In progress`, `In review`, `Done`.
6. Fill in the fields for the six sub-issues. Copy the values from the [example backlog](../../project-management/backlog.md#e01).

::: {.callout-caution}
Change the Status options before you rely on the Project workflows. A workflow that used a renamed option stops with an error. Open **Workflows** and select the new option again.
:::

{{< screenshot x3-workflows-broken >}}

### Create the three views

1. Rename the first view to `Backlog`. It stays a table.
2. Click **New view**, select **Board**, and name it `Board`. Type `-label:kind:epic` in the filter so that only tasks and stories appear.
3. Click **New view**, select **Roadmap**, and name it `Roadmap`.
4. In the Roadmap, click **Date fields**. Select `Start date` under **Start date** and `Target date` under **Target date**.
5. Click **Markers** and select **Milestone**. Set the zoom to **Quarter**.
6. Click **View**, then **Save view**, then **Save** in the confirmation dialog.

{{< screenshot x3-roadmap-date-fields >}}

{{< screenshot x3-roadmap >}}

### Record the dependency

1. Open `E01-T3 Submit the thesis registration to the Dean's Office`.
2. In the sidebar, open **Relationships**.
3. Select **Mark as blocked by** and choose `E01-T1`.
4. Optional: mark `E08-T3` as blocked by `E08-T2`.

## Expected state

{{< screenshot x3-backlog >}}

{{< screenshot x3-board >}}

- [ ] Three milestones exist; each has a due date and a justification.
- [ ] The Project is linked to the repository and has the visibility you chose.
- [ ] The fields Status, Priority, Basis, Start date, and Target date exist; Status has the five options.
- [ ] The views Backlog, Board, and Roadmap exist; the Roadmap shows bars and the milestone markers.
- [ ] E01-T3 shows "Blocked by: E01-T1".

## If something goes wrong

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The roadmap shows "Your project needs at least one date or iteration field". | The view has no date fields selected. | Select the date fields in **Date fields**. |
| The view settings are lost after a reload. | The confirmation was not saved. | Click **View → Save view**, then **Save** in the dialog. A blue dot means unsaved changes. |
| Workflows show a red error icon. | A Status option was renamed or removed. | Open **Workflows**, edit the workflow, and select an existing option. |
| The Project does not appear in the repository. | It is not linked. | **Projects** tab → **Link a project**. |
| No **Relationships** option. | The interface varies. | Open the Issue menu or use the [showcase](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) to compare. |
| Time runs out. | — | Use the fast route (**Make a copy**). |

## Alternatives

- **Pair:** one person builds the fields and views; the other creates the milestones and the dependency.
- **Private path:** set the Project to private. Project visibility does not follow the repository visibility.
